name.text: AROC in context - value and sign interpretation (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
{@contextintro@}

\[ {@fname@}({@ivar@}) = {@fdisp@} \]

where {@varmeaning@}.

Consider the interval from \( {@ivar@} = {@pp@} \) to \( {@ivar@} = {@qq@} \).

(a) Find the average rate of change of {@quantity@} over this interval, giving your answer exactly.

\( \text{Average rate of change} = \) [[input:ans1]] {@rateunit@} [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]
(b) Over this interval, is {@quantity@} increasing or decreasing? [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]
[[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The average rate of change of a function \(f\) over an interval \([p,q]\) is the slope of the secant line joining the two points on its graph:

\[ \text{AROC} = \frac{f(q) - f(p)}{q - p}. \]

Here \(f({@pp@}) = {@fp@}\) and \(f({@qq@}) = {@fq@}\), so

\[ \text{AROC} = \frac{ {@fq@} - ({@fp@}) }{ {@qq@} - {@pp@} } = \frac{ {@fq-fp@} }{ {@qq-pp@} } = {@ta1@}\ \text{@rateunit@} \]

Because the average rate of change is {@signword@} \(0\), {@quantity@} is {@dirword@} on average over this interval. {@interpretsentence@}

node.description: Divided by q instead of (q - p).

truefeedback.text: Check your denominator. The average rate of change divides the change in output by the change in input, \( q - p \), not by \( q \) alone.

node.description: Sign slip in the numerator (f(p) - f(q)).

truefeedback.text: Your value has the right size but the wrong sign. Keep the order consistent: the numerator is \( f(q) - f(p) \) over the denominator \( q - p \).

falsefeedback.text: Evaluate \(f\) at each endpoint, then compute \( \dfrac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p} \). Substitute carefully and try again.

node.description: Correct increasing/decreasing choice (ties to sign of AROC).

falsefeedback.text: Compare the sign of your average rate of change with \(0\). A positive average rate of change means the quantity is increasing on average; a negative one means it is decreasing. Match your choice to the sign of your answer in part (a).

qtest.description: Both correct: exact AROC and the matching direction.
Divided by q instead of (q - p); direction still correct.
Sign slip in the numerator; also picks the wrong direction.
